dawsassetCaseStudy.title: DawsAsset
dawsassetCaseStudy.subtitle: Shared asset-management platform delivered to production during a seven-week software engineering internship at Dawson College.

overview.title: Overview
overview.body: During a seven-week software engineering internship in April and May 2026, our team delivered a shared asset-management platform for Dawson College. Built on Odoo 17, DawsAsset replaced spreadsheet-based tracking for serialized equipment and consumable inventory across four departments: Computer Science, Radiation Oncology, Mechanical Engineering Technologies, and Civil Engineering Technology.

technicalHighlights.title: Technical Highlights
technicalHighlights.intro: Technologies and operational practices used throughout the project.

problem.title: The Problem
problem.body: Before DawsAsset, inventory was managed independently by multiple departments using spreadsheets and manual processes. This made it difficult to maintain a consistent view of assets while still supporting each department''s unique workflow. The goal was to replace those disconnected systems with a shared platform that could manage both serialized equipment and consumable inventory without forcing every department into the same process.

requirements.title: Requirements Engineering
requirements.body: Rather than working from a fixed specification, we collaborated directly with four departments to understand their existing inventory workflows and identify operational pain points. Those findings became the foundation for workflow diagrams, user stories, and implementable requirements. This involved preparing stakeholder interviews, analyzing existing inventory datasets, documenting findings, and reconciling different departmental workflows within one shared platform.

capabilities.title: Platform Capabilities
capabilities.intro: The delivered platform combined department-specific workflows with shared operational foundations.

assetTracking.title: Equipment and inventory
assetTracking.body: Managed serialized assets with barcode generation, scanning, and printing alongside consumable inventory, reorder rules, and kit verification audits.

loans.title: Loans and sessions
loans.body: Supported equipment checkout, overdue detection, condition tracking, in-lab usage sessions, and high-volume bulk actions.

studentKiosk.title: Student kiosk
studentKiosk.body: Let students self-serve checkout, returns, and lab sessions using an ID and equipment barcode, with damage and near-miss reporting.

guidedWorkflows.title: Guided workflows
guidedWorkflows.body: Supported multi-step workflows for equipment registration, stock receiving, interdepartmental transfers, and semester reports.

accessControl.title: Department access control
accessControl.body: Scoped chairs, teachers, lab technicians, and read-only users to their department's inventory while preserving local autonomy.

notifications.title: Operational notifications
notifications.body: Delivered low-stock, damage, and maintenance reminders through Dawson-branded email, Odoo Discuss, and record activities.

role.title: My Role
role.intro: DawsAsset was a team effort by Talon Dunbar, Diego Bouda, and Massi Djaiz, supervised by Victor Ponce. I served as the team''s primary stakeholder communicator while leading the project''s infrastructure, deployment planning, and technical documentation. I also maintained much of the project planning in GitLab and helped translate departmental needs into implementable requirements.
role.item1: Led stakeholder discovery and communication across four departments.
role.item2: Prepared requirements meetings, analyzed existing inventory data, and translated findings into user stories.
role.item3: Maintained project planning through GitLab issues, labels, and milestone tracking.
role.item4: Designed the infrastructure approach and coordinated staging and production deployment.
role.item5: Planned backups, testing, documentation, and final handoff.

delivery.title: Delivery Timeline
delivery.intro: The seven-week internship followed a week-by-week delivery path. Discovery, implementation, feedback, and deployment activities sometimes overlapped as the project evolved.
delivery.step1Description: VM setup, Docker environment, project planning, stakeholder preparation, and architecture proposal.
delivery.step2Description: Stakeholder meetings, inventory analysis, user stories, and department requirements.
delivery.step3Description: Initial Odoo modules, Computer Science workflows, and equipment tracking.
delivery.step4Description: Mechanical and Civil Engineering workflows, demonstrations, and feature iteration.
delivery.step5Description: User experience improvements, workflow refinement, QA deployment, and documentation.
delivery.step6Description: Stakeholder testing, bug fixes, deployment validation, and final refinements.
delivery.step7Description: Presented the completed platform to college leadership, project supervisors, and departmental representatives, demonstrating its operational value before completing production delivery and project handoff.

engineering.title: Operational Responsibilities
engineering.intro: Infrastructure, deployment, testing, documentation, and operational handoff were treated as core parts of the project lifecycle.

projectCoordination.title: Project coordination
projectCoordination.body: Maintained GitLab issues, labels, milestones, schedules, and project documentation to keep the team aligned.

infrastructure.title: Infrastructure and deployment
infrastructure.body: Helped establish the VM and Docker-based environment and supported staging, testing, and production delivery.

requirements.title: Requirements engineering
requirements.body: Prepared stakeholder interviews, analyzed inventory data, and translated findings into implementable requirements.

documentation.title: Documentation
documentation.body: Produced technical and operational documentation so the receiving team could understand, deploy, and maintain the delivered system.

stakeholders.title: Stakeholder coordination
stakeholders.body: Translated the needs of four departments into requirements for one shared platform while preserving their distinct workflows.

handoff.title: Maintainable handoff
handoff.body: Delivered the system with the documentation, backup planning, and operational context needed to reduce dependence on the internship team.

challenges.title: Challenges
challenges.item1: Gathering and clarifying requirements across four departments.
challenges.item2: Reconciling different inventory workflows within one shared platform.
challenges.item3: Moving from discovery to delivery within a seven-week internship.
challenges.item4: Completing documentation and handoff without leaving the system dependent on the internship team.

impact.title: Impact
impact.item1: A shared inventory platform across four Dawson College departments.
impact.item2: Serialized equipment and consumable inventory supported in the same system.
impact.item3: Delivered, documented, and handed off within seven weeks.
impact.item4: The platform remains in production at Dawson College following project handoff.
impact.item5: Presented the delivered platform and its operational value to college leadership and department stakeholders.

takeaways.title: Engineering Lessons
takeaways.body: This internship reinforced that successful software delivery extends beyond implementation. Stakeholder communication, requirements discovery, deployment planning, testing, backups, documentation, and handoff all contributed to a system that teams could successfully adopt and operate. It also showed me how much real-world delivery depends on navigating institutional constraints and incomplete information.
